title: Players in a table
description:
Players are records of three qwords, described by this `struc` (put it in your code):

```nasm
struc player
    .id:    resq 1
    .hp:    resq 1
    .score: resq 1
endstruc
```

Write:

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `total_score(players, count)` | the sum of every player's score |
| `best_id(players, count)` | the id of the player with the highest score (the first one on a tie); 0 when count is 0 |

Use the field names (`player.score`) and `player_size`, not raw numbers.

starter.solution.asm:
struc player
    .id:    resq 1
    .hp:    resq 1
    .score: resq 1
endstruc

total_score:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

best_id:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
struc player
    .id:    resq 1
    .hp:    resq 1
    .score: resq 1
endstruc

total_score:
        xor     eax, eax
.loop:  test    rsi, rsi
        jz      .done
        add     rax, [rdi + player.score]
        add     rdi, player_size
        dec     rsi
        jmp     .loop
.done:  ret

best_id:
        xor     eax, eax
        test    rsi, rsi
        jz      .done
        mov     rax, [rdi + player.id]
        mov     rdx, [rdi + player.score]
.loop:  add     rdi, player_size
        dec     rsi
        jz      .done
        mov     rcx, [rdi + player.score]
        cmp     rcx, rdx
        jle     .loop
        mov     rdx, rcx
        mov     rax, [rdi + player.id]
        jmp     .loop
.done:  ret

hints: Step a pointer through the array: after handling one record, `add rdi, player_size` moves it to the next. Each field is then `[rdi + player.field]`.
rules: Reach the score with its field name, player.score.
Step through the array with player_size.
